content: Paeonia lactiflora, commonly known as the Chinese Peony (referred to as 芍 or 白芍 in Chinese, with bái meaning white), is a herbaceous perennial flowering plant belonging to the family Paeoniaceae. It is native to central and eastern Asia, spanning from eastern Tibet through northern China to eastern Siberia. The plant typically grows to a height of 60 to 100 cm and features large, compound leaves measuring 20 to 40 cm in length. The flower buds of Paeonia lactiflora are large and rounded, eventually blooming into flowers with a diameter of 8 to 16 cm. These flowers typically have 5 to 10 petals, which can be white, pink, or crimson, and are accompanied by yellow stamens. In traditional Chinese medicine, this plant is referred to as 芍药 (sháo yào) or 白芍药 (bái sháo yào), and its root is utilized for its medicinal properties. The root is known to reduce fever and alleviate pain, as well as to stop bleeding and prevent infection when applied to wounds. Additionally, an antispasmodic effect of this plant is documented in the Japanese pharmacopoeia. Paeonia lactiflora is also widely cultivated as an ornamental plant in gardens, with several hundred selected cultivars available. Many of these cultivars feature double flowers, where the stamens are modified into additional petals. However, in China, the ornamental value of Paeonia lactiflora is considered less significant compared to the tree peony cultivars, such as Paeonia rockii (known as ziban mǔdān in Chinese) and its hybrid Paeonia × suffruticosa (referred to as mǔdān, 牡丹). The cultivars of Paeonia lactiflora are classified into three groups based on their floral structure: 1. Single-flowered cultivars: These have petals arranged in a single row, with fertile stamens. They resemble the wild type but are usually larger. 2. Japanese-flowered cultivars: These have petals arranged in a single or double row, with stamens transformed into sterile staminodes. 3. Double-flowered cultivars: In these, all or most of the stamens are transformed into petals. Examples of specific cultivars include: Paeonia lactiflora 'White Wings': A single-flowered cultivar. Paeonia lactiflora 'Doreen': A Japanese-flowered cultivar. Paeonia lactiflora 'Mons. Jules Elie': A double-flowered cultivar. Synonyms for Paeonia lactiflora include Paeonia albiflora, Paeonia chinensis, Paeonia edulis, Paeonia fragrans, Paeonia lactea, Paeonia reevesiana, and Paeonia.
